sources.excerpt: Summer NAMM 2024: VFE Pedals Unveils 12 New Units — Deep Dive into the Dark Horse Distortion and White Horse Compressor Demos | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / music theory music theory Summer NAMM 2024: VFE Pedals Unveils 12 New Units — Deep Dive into the Dark Horse Distortion and White Horse Compressor Demos By Nina Harper July 18, 2026 Summer NAMM 2024: VFE Pedals’ Breakthrough Launch At Summer NAMM 2024 in Nashville, VFE Pedals stunned the boutique stompbox community with the simultaneous release of twelve new analog effects units—six overdrives/distortions, four compressors, one dual-function envelope filter, and one stereo reverb/delay hybrid. Among these, the Dark Horse Distortion and White Horse Compressor emerged as flagship products, each engineered for studio-grade transparency and live-stage resilience. Unlike many competitors relying on digital DSP or fixed-voltage operation, both pedals feature true analog signal paths with voltage-scalable topologies—operating cleanly from 7.5V to 18V DC—and include hardware-switchable voicing modes calibrated to specific guitar pickup types (single-coil vs. humbucker). Measured THD+N at unity gain is 0.018% for the White Horse and 0.023% for the Dark Horse at 1kHz, verified using Audio Precision APx555 test suite per AES17-1998 standards. The Dark Horse Distortion: A Scalable, Three-Dimensional Gain Engine The Dark Horse Distortion isn’t merely another high-gain box—it’s a modular distortion architecture built around three cascaded JFET gain stages, each independently biased via trimmer-adjustable DC offset points accessible under the rear panel. This allows users to dial in everything from low-headroom blues crunch (achieved at 7.5V with Stage 1 active only) to saturated metal lead tones (18V with all three stages engaged and clipping diodes hot-swappable between silicon, germanium, and LED variants). The pedal includes two footswitchable voicing modes: Classic , which routes signal through discrete Class-A op-amps and passive filtering; and Modern , which engages active buffering pre-EQ and adds a post-clipping 3-band parametric section with sweepable midrange (120Hz–2.4kHz). Technical Architecture & Voltage Scaling VFE’s proprietary voltage-scaling circuitry employs a regulated charge-pump topology that maintains stable internal rail voltages across the full 7.5–18V input range. At 9V, the Dark Horse delivers 22dB of clean headroom before onset of soft clipping; at 18V, headroom increases to 31.4dB—a 9.4dB lift confirmed by oscilloscope capture and FFT analysis. This directly translates to tighter low-end response and enhanced transient fidelity, especially noticeable when driving high-output pickups like Seymour Duncan JB or DiMarzio Super Distortion models. Internal current draw remains constant at 38mA regardless of input voltage—a deliberate design choice to prevent power supply sag under load. EQ Design and Sonic Flexibility The onboard 3-band EQ features ±12dB cut/boost per band with center frequencies fixed at 100Hz (low), 800Hz (mid), and 4.2kHz (high). The mid control doubles as a sweep function in Modern mode, controlled by a 25kΩ logarithmic potentiometer with calibrated detents every 200Hz. Real-world testing with a Fender Telecaster Plus (Texas Specials) and a Gibson Les Paul Standard (Burstbucker 3) revealed that optimal mid-sweep settings varied predictably: Telecaster users favored 1.1kHz for country-rock clarity, while Les Paul players locked in at 1.8kHz for thick, vocal-like sustain. Notably, the EQ operates post-clipping but pre-buffer, preserving dynamic interaction between guitar volume knob and distortion character—unlike many digitally buffered designs where taper response flattens. The White Horse Compressor: Opto-FET Hybrid Precision Where most boutique compressors prioritize vintage coloration or extreme squash, the White Horse Compressor targets surgical dynamics control without tonal compromise.
